newsitem.title: UK: EMAP shares up on above-forecast H1 profit.
newsitem.headline: EMAP shares up on above-forecast H1 profit.

text.p: Shares in British publishing group EMAP rose in a flat market on Monday after the company reported first-half pretax profit above expectations.
EMAP shares were marked 8-1/2p higher at 731p in pre-market trade. Pretax profit before exceptional items rose to 50.6 million stg in the first half from 37.8 million a year earlier.
Analysts had expected pretax profits of between 43.5 million stg and 49.0 million.
"They were a very nice set of figures indeed and well above average forecasts," one marketmaker said.

"These were very strong figures, with underlying growth at consumer magazines and radio particularly strong...I would expect that to continue into the second half, helped by the drop in paper prices," said one analyst, who asked not to be named.
The analyst said EMAP's French consumer magazines business was benefiting from economies of scale and margins, into double digits, were expected to move ahead.

"The French performance is particularly pleasing because underlying revenues were down five percent but profit in underlying terms was slightly ahead, which, given the economic climate in France at present, is reassuring," he said.
The analyst played down the recent boardroom rift, which has weighed on EMAP shares.
"That friction was always there and has been going on for a considerable period...It might have even helped the company get business done. I think it is dying down now, though," he said.
